question: Who among the following established a unit of horsepower that is equal to one horse doing 33,000 foot - pounds of work in one minute?
solution:
The correct answer is **James Watt**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **James Watt** was a Scottish inventor and mechanical engineer.
 
• He is best known for his work on the **steam engine**, which played a crucial role in the Industrial Revolution.
 
• Watt introduced the concept of **horsepower** to quantify the power of engines.
 
• One unit of horsepower is defined as one horse doing **33,000 foot-pounds of work** in one minute.
 
• His improvements to the steam engine significantly increased its efficiency and utility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Term
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Horsepower**
 A unit of power that measures the rate at which work is done. Defined as 33,000 foot-pounds per minute.
 
 

 **Steam Engine**
 A heat engine that performs mechanical work using steam as its working fluid. Improved by James Watt.
 
 

 **Industrial Revolution**
 A period of major industrialization that took place during the late 1700s and early 1800s.
 
 

 **Foot-Pound**
 A unit of work in the English system, representing the work done by a force of one pound acting through a distance of one foot.
 
 

 **Efficiency**
 The ratio of the useful work performed by a machine or in a process to the total energy expended.
